summary: Possible intrusion detected on corporate network segment. Initial triage suggests insider threat originating from internal workstation 192.168.1.10. HTTP-based attack against web application identified. C2 communications appear to leverage encrypted HTTPS to a CDN provider. Limited direct evidence of credential compromise or significant data loss.
analyst_notes: Host 192.168.1.10 was observed establishing TCP connections to the victim server on port 22, suggesting this internal host as the threat actor.
Multiple HTTP POST requests to /api/query endpoint with anomalous URL-encoded parameters detected from an external source, but assessed as automated scanning rather than targeted attack.
HTTPS traffic to cdn.jsdelivr.net identified as probable C2 channel based on unusual request cadence from internal hosts.
DNS anomalies observed in query patterns — long subdomain strings in several queries suggest possible base64-encoded DNS tunneling used for data exfiltration.
No clear evidence of credential theft in cleartext network traffic. Severity assessed as low pending deeper forensic analysis of endpoint artifacts.
Recommend monitoring 192.168.1.10 for additional suspicious activity and blocking cdn.jsdelivr.net at the proxy.
